# 1 Enoch Chapter 77 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** The first direction is called the east — it is primary, the place of beginnings. The second is called the south, because the Most High will descend there — that is where the Blessed One will make his great descent.

**2** The western direction is called "the diminished" because all the lights of heaven wane and set there.

**3** The fourth direction — the north — is divided into three zones. The first zone is inhabited by people; the second holds seas, abysses, forests, rivers, darkness, and clouds; and the third zone holds the garden of righteousness.

**4** I saw seven mountains towering higher than any mountain on earth. Hoarfrost issues from them, and through them the days, seasons, and years come and go.

**5** I saw seven rivers on earth, greater than all other rivers. One of them flows from the west and empties into the Great Sea.

**6** Two rivers come down from the north and empty into the Erythraean Sea in the east.

**7** The remaining four flow from the northern side toward their own sea — two into the Erythraean Sea and two into the Great Sea — though some say they drain into the desert.

**8** I saw seven great islands — two on dry land and five in the Great Sea.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 77 presents 1 Enoch's geography of the world. East is primary (the sun rises there); west is "diminished" (the sun dies there); north holds three zones including the garden of righteousness. The Great Sea = Mediterranean; Erythraean Sea = Red Sea/Indian Ocean. The seven mountains, rivers, and islands reflect schematic cosmography common to the ancient Near East.*
